claim: Rspo2 and Rspo4 were undetectable in developing kidneys
source: Although Rspo2 and Rspo4 were undetectable in developing kidneys (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A—source data 1), Rspo1 and Rspo3 could be found as early as E10.5 within SIX2+ renal progenitors (Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and Motamedi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and referenced source data

claim: Rspo1 and Rspo3 could be found as early as E10.5 within SIX2+ renal progenitors
source: Although Rspo2 and Rspo4 were undetectable in developing kidneys (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A—source data 1), Rspo1 and Rspo3 could be found as early as E10.5 within SIX2+ renal progenitors (Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and Motamedi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and citation to Motamedi et al., 2014

claim: Rspo3 marked only a proportion of SIX2 positive cells at E10.5
source: Interestingly, Rspo3 marked only a proportion of SIX2 positive cells, suggesting this population to be heterogeneous already at this early age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: The SIX2+ progenitor population is heterogeneous at E10.5
source: Interestingly, Rspo3 marked only a proportion of SIX2 positive cells, suggesting this population to be heterogeneous already at this early age (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Rspo3 is expressed in only a subset of SIX2+ cells

claim: At E14.5, Rspo1 was detected throughout the CM, PTA, within renal vesicles, and the proximal part of the comma- and S-shaped bodies
source: At E14.5, Rspo1 was detected throughout the CM, PTA, within renal vesicles, and the proximal part of the comma- and S-shaped bodies, but decreased upon podocyte differentiation (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Rspo1 expression decreased upon podocyte differentiation
source: At E14.5, Rspo1 was detected throughout the CM, PTA, within renal vesicles, and the proximal part of the comma- and S-shaped bodies, but decreased upon podocyte differentiation (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Rspo3 expression at E14.5 was restricted to uncommitted SIX2+ cells
source: By contrast, Rspo3 expression was restricted to uncommitted SIX2+ cells (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C), and what appeared to be low levels of expression within the cortical stroma (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-C

claim: Rspo3 showed low levels of expression within the cortical stroma at E14.5
source: By contrast, Rspo3 expression was restricted to uncommitted SIX2+ cells (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C), and what appeared to be low levels of expression within the cortical stroma (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Expression of Rspo3 within the most cortical population of stromal cells persisted in animals that carry a CM-specific deletion of Rspo3 (Six2:Cre, Rspo3fl/fl)
source: Indeed, expression within the most cortical population of stromal cells persisted in animals that carry a CM-specific deletion of Rspo3 (Six2:Cre, Rspo3fl/fl) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: By E18.5 Rspo3 was dramatically reduced in NPCs
source: Interestingly, by E18.5 Rspo3 was dramatically reduced in NPCs, but strongly expressed in the cortical stromal compartment (Figure 1Bii), indicating a shift of expression towards the stroma.
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1Bii

claim: By E18.5 Rspo3 was strongly expressed in the cortical stromal compartment
source: Interestingly, by E18.5 Rspo3 was dramatically reduced in NPCs, but strongly expressed in the cortical stromal compartment (Figure 1Bii), indicating a shift of expression towards the stroma.
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1Bii

claim: There is a shift of Rspo3 expression from NPCs towards the stroma between E14.5 and E18.5
source: Interestingly, by E18.5 Rspo3 was dramatically reduced in NPCs, but strongly expressed in the cortical stromal compartment (Figure 1Bii), indicating a shift of expression towards the stroma.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of expression patterns at E14.5 and E18.5

claim: Strong Rspo3 signal was detected in stromal cells lining ducts of the renal papilla
source: Strong Rspo3 signal was also detected in stromal cells lining ducts of the renal papilla (Figure 1Biii).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 1Biii

claim: Lack of Rspo1 is compatible with life
source: Lack of Rspo1 is compatible with life (Chassot et al., 2008) and kidneys isolated from knockout mice showed no discernible abnormalities (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chassot et al., 2008 and unpublished observations

claim: Kidneys isolated from Rspo1 knockout mice showed no discernible abnormalities
source: Lack of Rspo1 is compatible with life (Chassot et al., 2008) and kidneys isolated from knockout mice showed no discernible abnormalities (data not shown).
evidence: Based on unpublished observations by the authors

claim: Mice carrying a constitutive deletion of Rspo3 die at E9.5 due to placental defects
source: Mice carrying a constitutive deletion of Rspo3 die at E9.5 due to placental defects (Aoki et al., 2007; Kazanskaya et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aoki et al., 2007 and Kazanskaya et al., 2008

claim: Tamoxifen induction at E11.5 in presence of CAGG:CreERTM driver efficiently abolished Rspo3 expression 3 days after induction (E14.5)
source: Tamoxifen (Tam) induction at E11.5 in presence of the ubiquitously expressed CAGG:CreERTM driver (Hayashi and McMahon, 2002) efficiently abolished Rspo3 expression 3 days after induction (E14.5) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and citation to Hayashi and McMahon, 2002

claim: Tamoxifen-induced deletion of Rspo3 at E11.5 resulted in a mild reduction of progenitor cells at E14.5
source: Tamoxifen (Tam) induction at E11.5 in presence of the ubiquitously expressed CAGG:CreERTM driver (Hayashi and McMahon, 2002) efficiently abolished Rspo3 expression 3 days after induction (E14.5) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and resulted in a mild reduction of progenitor cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B

claim: Depletion of Rspo1 and Rspo3 was efficient in double mutant kidneys
source: Depletion was efficient, and no compensatory up-regulation of Rspo2 or Rspo4 was detected in double mutant kidneys (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: No compensatory up-regulation of Rspo2 or Rspo4 was detected in Rspo1/Rspo3 double mutant kidneys
source: Depletion was efficient, and no compensatory up-regulation of Rspo2 or Rspo4 was detected in double mutant kidneys (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: R-spondin double mutant (DM) embryos showed severe renal hypoplasia at E18.5
source: Macroscopic observation at E18.5 showed severe renal hypoplasia in R-spondin DM, when compared to control littermates (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by macroscopic images shown in Figure 1C,D

claim: Hematoxylin and Eosin staining of kidneys at E14.5 indicated a reduced nephrogenic zone and a near-complete absence of nephrons in R-spondin DM
source: Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining of kidneys at E14.5 indicated a reduced nephrogenic zone and a near-complete absence of nephrons (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 1E

claim: Molecular analysis confirmed a dramatic loss of SIX2+ progenitors in R-spondin DM
source: Molecular analysis confirmed a dramatic loss of SIX2+ progenitors and an absence of forming nephrons (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 2A

claim: Molecular analysis confirmed an absence of forming nephrons in R-spondin DM
source: Molecular analysis confirmed a dramatic loss of SIX2+ progenitors and an absence of forming nephrons (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 2A

claim: The remaining SIX2-positive cells in R-spondin DM appeared scattered, when compared to the condensed mesenchyme seen in controls
source: The remaining SIX2-positive cells appeared scattered, when compared to the condensed mesenchyme seen in controls.
evidence: Based on observations from immunofluorescent analysis

claim: A similar loss of NPCs was observed when R-spondin deletion was induced at E10.5, E12.5 or E13.5
source: A similar loss of NPCs was observed when R-spondin deletion was induced at E10.5, E12.5 or E13.5 indicating a continuous requirement of these signalling molecules for the maintenance of the NPC pool (data not shown).
evidence: Based on unpublished observations by the authors

claim: R-spondin signalling molecules are continuously required for the maintenance of the NPC pool
source: A similar loss of NPCs was observed when R-spondin deletion was induced at E10.5, E12.5 or E13.5 indicating a continuous requirement of these signalling molecules for the maintenance of the NPC pool (data not shown).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that deletion at multiple time points produces similar phenotypes

claim: Quantification of BrdU-labelled SIX2+ progenitors indicated a 40% reduction of proliferation in the progenitor compartment (p=0.0003)
source: Quantification of BrdU-labelled SIX2+ progenitors indicated a 40% reduction of proliferation in this compartment (p=0.0003) (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by BrdU labeling quantification shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—source data 1

claim: A significant 8.1 fold increase of apoptosis among the SIX2+ cells located in the CM was observed (p=0.0319)
source: In addition, a significant 8.1 fold increase of apoptosis among the SIX2+ cells located in the CM was observed (p=0.0319) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by TUNEL analysis shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—source data 1

claim: Ubiquitous deletion of R-spondins caused a general downregulation of Axin2 already 2 days after tamoxifen induction
source: Ubiquitous deletion of R-spondins caused a general downregulation of Axin2 already 2 days after tamoxifen induction, an observation consistent with a loss of WNT/β–catenin signalling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by RNAScope analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D

claim: Downregulation of Axin2 upon R-spondin deletion is consistent with a loss of WNT/β–catenin signalling
source: Ubiquitous deletion of R-spondins caused a general downregulation of Axin2 already 2 days after tamoxifen induction, an observation consistent with a loss of WNT/β–catenin signalling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Inferred from the known role of Axin2 as a direct downstream target of β-catenin signalling

claim: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin (Six2:Cre; Ctnnb1fl/fl) resulted in a dramatic reduction (93%; p<0.0001) of SIX2+ progenitor cells
source: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin (Six2:Cre; Ctnnb1fl/fl) phenocopied the Rspo1/3 DM phenotype with a dramatic reduction (93%; p<0.0001) of SIX2+ progenitor cells and a near-complete block of nephron formation as indicated by an almost complete absence of the nephron specific marker JAG1 (Figure 2D and E; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—source data 1

claim: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin resulted in a near-complete block of nephron formation
source: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin (Six2:Cre; Ctnnb1fl/fl) phenocopied the Rspo1/3 DM phenotype with a dramatic reduction (93%; p<0.0001) of SIX2+ progenitor cells and a near-complete block of nephron formation as indicated by an almost complete absence of the nephron specific marker JAG1 (Figure 2D and E; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin phenocopied the Rspo1/3 DM phenotype
source: Progenitor-specific deletion of β-catenin (Six2:Cre; Ctnnb1fl/fl) phenocopied the Rspo1/3 DM phenotype with a dramatic reduction (93%; p<0.0001) of SIX2+ progenitor cells and a near-complete block of nephron formation as indicated by an almost complete absence of the nephron specific marker JAG1 (Figure 2D and E; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by comparison of phenotypes shown in Figure 2D and E

claim: R-spondins are required for nephron progenitor maintenance via the activation of canonical β-catenin signalling
source: Taken together these data indicate a requirement of R-spondins for nephron progenitor maintenance via the activation of canonical β-catenin signalling.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotypic similarity between R-spondin and β-catenin deletion mutants

claim: At E14.5, Foxd1:Cre-DM kidneys appeared normal and showed a comparable number of SIX2+ cells per section when compared to control littermates (p=0.7887)
source: At E14.5, Foxd1:Cre-DM kidneys appeared normal and showed a comparable number of SIX2+ cells per section when compared to control littermates (p=0.7887; Figure 3C; Figure 3—source data 1 and data not shown).
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—source data 1

claim: At E18.5 Foxd1:Cre-DM mutant kidneys were hypoplastic
source: By contrast, at E18.5 mutant kidneys were hypoplastic (Figure 3B) and displayed a reduction of the nephrogenic zone associated with a significant loss of SIX2+ progenitor cells (p=0.0167) (Figure 3D–F; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by macroscopic images shown in Figure 3B

claim: At E18.5 Foxd1:Cre-DM mutant kidneys displayed a reduction of the nephrogenic zone associated with a significant loss of SIX2+ progenitor cells (p=0.0167)
source: By contrast, at E18.5 mutant kidneys were hypoplastic (Figure 3B) and displayed a reduction of the nephrogenic zone associated with a significant loss of SIX2+ progenitor cells (p=0.0167) (Figure 3D–F; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—source data 1, and histological analysis in Figure 3E-F

claim: Continuous expression of Rspo3 from the stromal compartment is required to maintain progenitor cells at later stages of kidney formation
source: We conclude that continuous expression of Rspo3 from the stromal compartment is required to maintain progenitor cells at later stages of kidney formation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that stromal-specific deletion of Rspo3 leads to progenitor loss at E18.5 but not E14.5

claim: At E18.5 Six2:Cre-DM embryos had hypodysplastic kidneys
source: At E18.5 Six2:Cre-DM embryos had hypodysplastic kidneys that histologically displayed defects in nephrogenesis and a complete absence of glomeruli (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by macroscopic and histological images shown in Figure 4B

claim: Six2:Cre-DM kidneys histologically displayed defects in nephrogenesis and a complete absence of glomeruli
source: At E18.5 Six2:Cre-DM embryos had hypodysplastic kidneys that histologically displayed defects in nephrogenesis and a complete absence of glomeruli (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4B

claim: Histological and immunofluorescent analysis of E14.5 Six2:Cre-DM kidneys revealed the persistence of SIX2+ progenitors albeit at slightly lower numbers
source: Histological and immunofluorescent analysis of E14.5 kidneys confirmed this observation and revealed the persistence of SIX2+ progenitors albeit at slightly lower numbers (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: Staining for JAG1 and WT1 demonstrated a complete absence of epithelial nephrons and podocytes in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys
source: Importantly, staining for JAG1 and WT1 demonstrated a complete absence of epithelial nephrons and podocytes, respectively, indicating an essential role for R-spondin1/3 in nephron differentiation.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: R-spondin1/3 have an essential role in nephron differentiation
source: Importantly, staining for JAG1 and WT1 demonstrated a complete absence of epithelial nephrons and podocytes, respectively, indicating an essential role for R-spondin1/3 in nephron differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of differentiated nephron structures in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys

claim: Loss of R-spondins did not impact Wnt9b expression
source: In situ hybridisation (ISH) analysis revealed that loss of R-spondins did not impact Wnt9b expression (Figure 4Di and ii), but dramatically reduced the expression of Class II (Bmp7, Tfrc, Crym1, Uncx4, Etv5 and Slc12a) target genes within progenitors (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4Di and ii

claim: Loss of R-spondins dramatically reduced the expression of Class II (Bmp7, Tfrc, Crym1, Uncx4, Etv5 and Slc12a) target genes within progenitors
source: In situ hybridisation (ISH) analysis revealed that loss of R-spondins did not impact Wnt9b expression (Figure 4Di and ii), but dramatically reduced the expression of Class II (Bmp7, Tfrc, Crym1, Uncx4, Etv5 and Slc12a) target genes within progenitors (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C

claim: Tfrc was absent from mesenchymal cells in Six2:Cre-DM, but was maintained to be expressed in the ureteric epithelium
source: Interestingly, Tfrc was absent from mesenchymal cells, but was maintained to be expressed in the ureteric epithelium suggesting that progenitor-specific R-spondin expression is dispensable for its activation in the collecting duct system.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization observations

claim: Progenitor-specific R-spondin expression is dispensable for Tfrc activation in the collecting duct system
source: Interestingly, Tfrc was absent from mesenchymal cells, but was maintained to be expressed in the ureteric epithelium suggesting that progenitor-specific R-spondin expression is dispensable for its activation in the collecting duct system.
evidence: Inferred from the persistence of Tfrc expression in ureteric epithelium despite progenitor-specific deletion

claim: The class I target Wnt4 was undetectable within the nephrogenic zone in Six2:Cre-DM
source: The class I target Wnt4, a key regulator of MET (Stark et al., 1994), was also undetectable within the nephrogenic zone, but remained expressed in medullary stromal cells (Figure 4D ix and x).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4D ix and x

claim: Wnt4 remained expressed in medullary stromal cells in Six2:Cre-DM
source: The class I target Wnt4, a key regulator of MET (Stark et al., 1994), was also undetectable within the nephrogenic zone, but remained expressed in medullary stromal cells (Figure 4D ix and x).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4D ix and x

claim: Wnt4 is a key regulator of MET
source: The class I target Wnt4, a key regulator of MET (Stark et al., 1994), was also undetectable within the nephrogenic zone, but remained expressed in medullary stromal cells (Figure 4D ix and x).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stark et al., 1994

claim: The direct downstream target Axin2 was 51% down regulated in the nephrogenic zone of Six2:Cre-DM mutant kidneys (p<0.0001)
source: Consistent with a requirement of R-spondins for β-catenin activation, the direct downstream target Axin2 was 51% down regulated in the nephrogenic zone of mutant kidneys (p<0.0001, Figure 4E; Figure 4—source data 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope quantification shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—source data 1

claim: R-spondins are required for β-catenin activation
source: Consistent with a requirement of R-spondins for β-catenin activation, the direct downstream target Axin2 was 51% down regulated in the nephrogenic zone of mutant kidneys (p<0.0001, Figure 4E; Figure 4—source data 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Inferred from the downregulation of Axin2, a direct β-catenin target, upon R-spondin deletion

claim: Six2:Cre-DM kidneys showed a small reduction of nephron progenitors
source: Six2:Cre-DM kidneys showed a small reduction of nephron progenitors (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 4C

claim: Wt1:CreERT2-DM embryos kidneys contained large numbers of SIX2+ progenitors
source: Wt1:CreERT2-DM embryos kidneys contained large numbers of SIX2+ progenitors (Figure 5Bi and ii) that failed to differentiate.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 5Bi and ii

claim: Wt1:CreERT2-DM progenitors failed to differentiate
source: Wt1:CreERT2-DM embryos kidneys contained large numbers of SIX2+ progenitors (Figure 5Bi and ii) that failed to differentiate.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of differentiation markers

claim: Expression of LEF1 was virtually absent from the nephrogenic region of Rspo1/3 double mutant mice
source: Indeed, expression of LEF1, a direct target and interaction partner of β-catenin that is also a marker of committed pretubular aggregates, was virtually absent from the nephrogenic region of Rspo1/3 double mutant mice (Figure 5Biii and iv).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescent analysis shown in Figure 5Biii and iv

claim: LEF1 is a direct target and interaction partner of β-catenin
source: Indeed, expression of LEF1, a direct target and interaction partner of β-catenin that is also a marker of committed pretubular aggregates, was virtually absent from the nephrogenic region of Rspo1/3 double mutant mice (Figure 5Biii and iv).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

claim: LEF1 is a marker of committed pretubular aggregates
source: Indeed, expression of LEF1, a direct target and interaction partner of β-catenin that is also a marker of committed pretubular aggregates, was virtually absent from the nephrogenic region of Rspo1/3 double mutant mice (Figure 5Biii and iv).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

claim: Six2:Cre and Wt1:CreERT2 driven deletion showed a very similar phenotype
source: Six2:Cre and Wt1:CreERT2 driven deletion thus showed a very similar phenotype.
evidence: Based on comparison of phenotypes described in the manuscript

claim: The higher number of progenitors in WT1:CreERT2-induced mutants is likely due to less efficient deletion of Rspo3 and, as a consequence, persistence of slightly higher levels of R-spondin activity
source: The higher number of progenitors in WT1:CreERT2-induced mutants is likely due to less efficient deletion of Rspo3 and, as a consequence, persistence of slightly higher levels of R-spondin activity.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on observed differences between Cre lines

claim: Gene expression analysis after 48 hr revealed a 2.3-fold and 4.6-fold increase for the β-catenin targets Axin2 and Wnt4, respectively, after combined treatment with WNT3A and RSPO3
source: Gene expression analysis after 48 hr revealed a 2.3-fold and 4.6-fold increase for the β-catenin targets Axin2 and Wnt4, respectively, after combined treatment (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 1

claim: Treatment with recombinant WNT3A alone did not have an effect on Axin2 or Wnt4 expression in isolated NPCs
source: Interestingly, treatment with recombinant WNT3A alone did not have an effect suggesting that WNT/β-catenin signalling is actively suppressed in this cell type and crucially requires R-spondin action to permit activation of this pathway (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5D

claim: WNT/β-catenin signalling is actively suppressed in nephron progenitor cells and crucially requires R-spondin action to permit activation of this pathway
source: Interestingly, treatment with recombinant WNT3A alone did not have an effect suggesting that WNT/β-catenin signalling is actively suppressed in this cell type and crucially requires R-spondin action to permit activation of this pathway (Figure 5D).
evidence: Inferred from the observation that WNT3A alone is insufficient to activate β-catenin targets, but combined WNT3A and RSPO3 treatment is effective

claim: Commitment of renal progenitors to nephron differentiation involves canonical BMP7 signalling
source: Commitment of renal progenitors to nephron differentiation involves canonical BMP7 signalling, which allows cells to fully respond to the WNT/β−catenin pathway and undergo MET (Brown et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Brown et al., 2013

claim: Canonical BMP7 signalling allows cells to fully respond to the WNT/β−catenin pathway and undergo MET
source: Commitment of renal progenitors to nephron differentiation involves canonical BMP7 signalling, which allows cells to fully respond to the WNT/β−catenin pathway and undergo MET (Brown et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Brown et al., 2013

claim: In situ hybridization indicated a dramatic downregulation of Bmp7 in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys
source: In situ hybridization indicated a dramatic downregulation of Bmp7 in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4D

claim: Canonical BMP signalling induces phosphorylation of SMAD1/5
source: Canonical BMP signalling induces phosphorylation of SMAD1/5 and we therefore evaluated the phosphorylation status of this signal transducer.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

claim: Progenitors in control kidneys that engaged in MET were positive for pSMAD1/5
source: Whereas progenitors in control kidneys that engaged in MET were positive for pSMAD1/5 (Figure 5E), the nephrogenic zone in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys showed a 88% reduction of staining (p<0.0001; Figure 5F; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 5E

claim: The nephrogenic zone in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys showed a 88% reduction of pSMAD1/5 staining (p<0.0001)
source: Whereas progenitors in control kidneys that engaged in MET were positive for pSMAD1/5 (Figure 5E), the nephrogenic zone in Six2:Cre-DM kidneys showed a 88% reduction of staining (p<0.0001; Figure 5F; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—source data 1

claim: pSMAD staining in medullary stroma was not affected by Six2:Cre-DM deletion
source: pSMAD staining in medullary stroma was not affected by this deletion.
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 5E

claim: R-spondins are required for Bmp7 activation, which in turn permits priming of renal progenitors for MET
source: Taken together these data demonstrate that R-spondins are required for Bmp7 activation, which in turn permits priming of renal progenitors for MET.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that R-spondin deletion leads to loss of Bmp7 expression and pSMAD1/5 phosphorylation

claim: RNF43 is specifically expressed within the branching ureter
source: Expression analysis using RNA-Scope demonstrated RNF43 to be specifically expressed within the branching ureter, whereas ZNRF3 showed a more widespread expression pattern, covering also the nephrogenic niche (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: ZNRF3 showed a more widespread expression pattern, covering also the nephrogenic niche
source: Expression analysis using RNA-Scope demonstrated RNF43 to be specifically expressed within the branching ureter, whereas ZNRF3 showed a more widespread expression pattern, covering also the nephrogenic niche (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: Mutations in Lgr4 or Lgr4/5 have been shown to have mild defects in kidney development
source: R-spondin interaction with ZNRF3/RNF43 is believed to be primarily mediated via binding to their cognate receptors LGR4-6 and mutations in Lgr4 or Lgr4/5 have been shown to have mild defects in kidney development (Kato et al., 2006; Dang et al., 2014; Kinzel et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kato et al., 2006; Dang et al., 2014; Kinzel et al., 2014

claim: Lgr4 showed the broadest expression pattern with mRNA detected in virtually all cell types of the developing kidney
source: Lgr4 showed the broadest expression pattern with mRNA detected in virtually all cell types of the developing kidney (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: Particularly strong Lgr4 staining was found in the distal part of comma shaped bodies that extended into the intermediate segment at the S-shaped body stage
source: Particularly, strong staining was found in the distal part of comma shaped bodies that extended into the intermediate segment at the S-shaped body stage.
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: Strong Lgr4 staining was detected in medullary stromal cells that line the developing ureter
source: In addition, we detected strong staining in medullary stromal cells that line the developing ureter.
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: Lgr5 mRNA was virtually absent from the CM
source: Lgr5 mRNA was virtually absent from the CM, but could be found within ureteric tips, a proportion of medullary stroma cells and the distal segment of S-shaped bodies, as previously reported using a lacZ reporter strain (Barker et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A and citation to Barker et al., 2012

claim: Lgr5 could be found within ureteric tips, a proportion of medullary stroma cells and the distal segment of S-shaped bodies
source: Lgr5 mRNA was virtually absent from the CM, but could be found within ureteric tips, a proportion of medullary stroma cells and the distal segment of S-shaped bodies, as previously reported using a lacZ reporter strain (Barker et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A and citation to Barker et al., 2012

claim: Lgr6 mRNA showed the most restricted expression pattern and could only be detected in PTAs of forming nephrons
source: Lgr6 mRNA showed the most restricted expression pattern and could only be detected in PTAs of forming nephrons (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-Scope analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: Quantification of SIX2-positive NPCs at E14.5 indicated a reduction by 37% (p=0.0006) in Lgr4-/- mutants compared to control kidneys
source: Quantification of SIX2-positive NPCs at E14.5 indicated a reduction by 37% (p=0.0006) in Lgr4-/-mutants compared to control kidneys (Figure 6B,C; Figure 6—source data 1), a cell loss that was considerably inferior to that observed in R-spondin mutants.
evidence: Supported by quantification shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—source data 1

claim: The cell loss in Lgr4-/- mutants was considerably inferior to that observed in R-spondin mutants
source: Quantification of SIX2-positive NPCs at E14.5 indicated a reduction by 37% (p=0.0006) in Lgr4-/-mutants compared to control kidneys (Figure 6B,C; Figure 6—source data 1), a cell loss that was considerably inferior to that observed in R-spondin mutants.
